svg.text: swift run TOMLClaimDemo (real output, captured twice, byte-identical)
$ swift run TOMLClaimDemo
TOMLClaimKit demo: checking what LLM answers say about TOML
Each block is parsed and each snippet run as Python's tomllib (TOML 1.0) would.
[1] python_version = 3.10 in pyproject.toml, said to stay "3.10"
answer: wrong (3 claims checked, 0 hold, 1 to check, 2 wrong)
check validity: [project] name = "inventory" requires-python = ">=3.10" [... is valid TOML [versionLikeFloats]
The TOML has unquoted numbers written with a trailing zero, which load without it: python_version = 3.10; quote any that must stay text,
such as a version.
WRONG reading: python_version = 3.10 -> the string "3.10" [trailingZeroDropped]
`python_version = 3.10` is not the string "3.10": tomllib reads it as the float 3.1 (an unquoted 3.10 is the float 3.1; quote it to keep
the text).
WRONG loading: print(data["tool"]["mypy"]["python_version"]) -> 3.10 [trailingZeroDropped]
`print(data["tool"]["mypy"]["python_version"])` gives 3.1, not 3.10 (an unquoted 3.10 is the float 3.1; quote it to keep the text).
feedback sent back to the model:
| Some of what your answer says about TOML does not hold:
| - The TOML has unquoted numbers written with a trailing zero, which load without it: python_version = 3.10; quote any that must stay text,
such as a version.
| - `python_version = 3.10` is not the string "3.10": tomllib reads it as the float 3.1 (an unquoted 3.10 is the float 3.1; quote it to keep
the text).
| - `print(data["tool"]["mypy"]["python_version"])` gives 3.1, not 3.10 (an unquoted 3.10 is the float 3.1; quote it to keep the text).
| Parse each block and run each snippet with tomllib, quote any value that must stay text, correct every statement that depends on it, and keep
the rest of the answer as it is.
rewrite: verified (3 claims checked, 3 hold)
ok validity: [project] name = "inventory" requires-python = ">=3.10" [... is valid TOML
ok reading: python_version = "3.10" -> the string "3.10"
ok loading: print(data["tool"]["mypy"]["python_version"]) -> 3.10
[2] tomllib.load on a text-mode file, and a dotted key looked up whole
answer: wrong (3 claims checked, 1 hold, 2 wrong)
ok validity: [tool.poetry] name = "inventory" version = "0.1.0" is shown as TOML
WRONG loading: tomllib.load(f) -> code that runs [textMode]
`tomllib.load(f)` raises TypeError: File must be opened in binary mode, e.g. use `open('foo.toml', 'rb')`; the answer uses it as if it
runs (tomllib.load needs a file opened in binary mode: open(path, "rb")).
WRONG loading: print(config["tool.poetry"]["version"]) -> 0.1.0 [dottedKeyLookup]
`print(config["tool.poetry"]["version"])` raises KeyError: 'tool.poetry'; the answer shows 0.1.0 (a dotted key makes nested tables, so
index one level at a time: data["tool"]["poetry"]).
rewrite: verified (2 claims checked, 2 hold)
ok validity: [tool.poetry] name = "inventory" version = "0.1.0" is shown as TOML
ok loading: print(config["tool"]["poetry"]["version"]) -> 0.1.0

[4] A table declared twice, a repeated key, and tomllib.dumps
answer: wrong (3 claims checked, 0 hold, 3 wrong)
WRONG validity: [server] host = "0.0.0.0" [server] port = 8080 is shown as TOML [duplicateTable]
The block shown as TOML does not parse: a table defined twice (server) at line 4, column 8 (TOML refuses a table declared twice; keep its
keys under one header).
WRONG loading: print(settings["port"]) -> 8080 [duplicateKey]
`print(settings["port"])` raises tomllib.TOMLDecodeError: a key defined twice (port) at line 2, column 12; the answer shows 8080 (tomllib
raises on a key defined twice rather than keeping either value).
WRONG loading: tomllib.dumps(settings) -> code that runs [noDumper]
`tomllib.dumps(settings)` raises AttributeError: module 'tomllib' has no attribute 'dumps'; the answer uses it as if it runs (tomllib
only reads TOML; write it with the tomli-w package (tomli_w.dumps)).
rewrite: verified (2 claims checked, 2 hold)
ok validity: [server] host = "0.0.0.0" port = 8080 is shown as TOML
ok loading: tomllib.loads('port = 8000\nport = 8080\n') -> TOMLDecodeError: Cannot overwrite a value
[5] What values read as: six sentences, three of them wrong
answer: wrong (6 claims checked, 3 hold, 3 wrong)
ok reading: timeout = 1e3 -> float
ok reading: mode = 0o755 -> the integer 493
ok reading: released = 2024-01-02 -> a `datetime.date`
WRONG reading: mode = 0755 -> the integer 755 [leadingZero]
`mode = 0755` is not the integer 755: tomllib refuses it: a decimal number with a leading zero (0755) (TOML refuses a decimal number with
a leading zero; write 0o755 for octal, or quote it).
WRONG reading: enabled = True -> boolean [capitalizedBoolean]
`enabled = True` is not boolean: tomllib refuses it: a boolean that is not lowercase `true` or `false` (True) (TOML booleans are
lowercase true and false).
WRONG reading: start = 09:30 -> time [dateFormat]
`start = 09:30` is not time: tomllib refuses it: a date or time not written as YYYY-MM-DD or HH:MM:SS (09:30) (TOML dates are YYYY-MM-DD
and times HH:MM:SS, seconds included).
lenient policy, same Poetry answer: wrong (1 claim checked, 0 hold, 1 wrong)
WRONG validity: [tool.poetry.dependencies] python = ^3.10 requests = "^2.... is valid TOML [bareString]
The text said to be valid TOML does not parse: unquoted text where TOML needs a quoted string (^3.10) at line 2, column 10 (TOML strings
need quotes: "..." or '...').
